newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Comm/Transport Ministry seeks more spending.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Comm/Transport Ministry seeks more spending.

text.p: Mexico's Communications and Transport Ministry plans to spend a little more than 12.6 billion pesos on capital investments in 1997 compared to 1996 spending of 12.349 billion pesos, Mininster Carlos Ruiz Sacristan said in a public forum on Tuesday.

"Of this investment, 70 percent will be destined for highway and road infrastructure, about 20 percent to (other) tranportation and about 10 percent to the telecommunications area," Ruiz told President Ernesto Zedillo, who was present for the ministry's presentation of its 1997 goals.
The government plans to repair more than 260 bridges and about 1,860 miles (3,000 km) of roads in poor condition of the more than 26,000 miles (42,000 km) of roads under the ministry's jurisdiction.

Deputy Minister of Infrastructure Manuel Rodriguez said the repairs are necessary because of earthquakes and hurricanes that have hit the country, and that most the projects will be contracted to private companies.

In addition, Ruiz said the ministry will continue auctioning the nation's sea ports, airports, railways and radio spectrum bands through 1997, with further details of the privatizations expected to be published within six months.

"In transportation, no effort will be sufficient if we cannot improve the channels of communication," Ruiz said. "In every area of the program, we have included specific actions that allow us to reduce the number of accidents and crimes and aspire to a transportation system in Mexico that reaches improved levels of trustworthiness and efficiency."
